report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/kairos/scheduler.py; docstring claims about gate_candidates, plan/dispatch separation, spawn, configure, and demo tasks are mostly kept or uncheckable within this chunk.
risks: gate_candidates docstring | medium | The docstring claims availability defaults to DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY, but DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY is not defined in this chunk; uncheckable here. | Check if DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY is defined elsewhere in the module.

gate_candidates docstring | medium | The docstring claims gate_candidates covers every TaskAttempt in this batch, but the actual function is imported and not shown; uncheckable. | Inspect gate_candidates implementation.
spawn docstring | medium | Docstring claims decompose uses a deterministic per-path fallback, but the decompose function is imported and not shown; uncheckable. | Inspect decompose implementation.
configure docstring | medium | Docstring claims routing picks up changes with no restart, but routing code is in another module; uncheckable. | Inspect router.load_agents.
configure docstring | medium | Docstring claims ValueError on invalid spec, but no validation is visible in this chunk; uncheckable. | Inspect create_role/update_role for validation.
main | low | The summary line in main says 'bounced back to Adam' but the plan may not have a 'bounced_to_adam' key; relies on plan's structure. | Check plan return shape.
main | low | The CLI prints a table with column widths; long objectives are truncated but not ellipsized, potentially misaligning columns. | Run with long objectives.
configure | low | If spec has no 'name', the code sets name=None and calls create_role; the returned summary includes 'role': None, which may be misleading. | Test with no name.

handoff.purpose: Review the second half of the scheduler module: gate_candidates wrapper, spawn, configure, demo tasks, and CLI main.

symbols.name: gate_candidates wrapper (method of KairosScheduler)
symbols.note: Accepts tasks, filters accepted write attempts, delegates to imported gate_candidates with bounded workers.

symbols.name: spawn
symbols.note: One-shot entry: decomposes objective, then plans (dry_run) or dispatches (live).

symbols.name: configure
symbols.note: Creates or updates an agent role via agents_registry; returns summary with action, role, path, config.

symbols.name: _demo_tasks
symbols.note: Converts benchmark TASKS into list of dicts with objective and paths.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry: parses args, creates scheduler, plans demo tasks, prints JSON or table.

claims.text: gate_candidates -- added here so this wrapper does not silently strip a capability that module already supports; see that function's own docstring for exactly what it covers (every TaskAttempt in this batch) and does not (the cumulative re-gate inside promote_candidates, a separate, filed follow-up, not this method's concern since it never promotes).
claims.why: The exact coverage of gate_candidates is not visible in this chunk; the wrapper simply calls the imported function.

claims.text: Landing a candidate this returns into repo_root is a SEPARATE, explicit act -- see promote_candidates and the comment on can_parallel in dispatch for why this method does not do that itself.
claims.why: The wrapper does not promote; it only returns gate_candidates' result. The rationale about can_parallel is in dispatch, not in this chunk.

claims.text: One-shot entry: decompose a single objective into subtasks, then plan (dry_run) or dispatch (live) them across the bounded local bench.
claims.why: spawn calls decompose, then returns plan if dry_run else dispatch with dry_run=False.

claims.text: This is the dynamic counterpart to the hardcoded _demo_tasks flow -- the subtasks come from decompose (local model with a deterministic per-path fallback), not a fixed list.
claims.why: The decompose function is imported; its fallback behavior is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Dynamic agent configurator: mint or reshape an agent-role definition at runtime.
claims.why: configure calls create_role or update_role on the agents_registry.

claims.text: Ikarus owns the crew roster, so creating/editing roles is his job -- routing (router.load_agents) picks up the change with no restart.
claims.why: The routing behavior is not in this chunk; the claim refers to another module.

claims.text: Returns a summary; raises ValueError on an invalid spec.
claims.why: The code returns a summary, but no validation is visible here; the ValueError would come from create_role/update_role.

claims.text: main: KAIROS spawn plan (local bench on, DeepSeek dormant)
claims.why: No evidence in this chunk about the bench or model state; it's just a print label.

claims.text: spawned N local worker(s) across M wave(s) (<= max_workers/wave); bounced B back to Adam.
claims.why: The plan structure (spawned, waves, bounced_to_adam) comes from plan(), which is not in this chunk.

observations.what: The gate_candidates wrapper uses DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY without it being defined in this chunk.
The spawn method uses decompose with repo_root, but the function signature is not visible here; the docstring mentions a deterministic per-path fallback.
configure returns 'role': name even when name is None (if spec lacks 'name'), which may be misleading.
main prints a table with fixed column widths; long objectives are truncated without ellipsis, potentially misaligning.
